title: Price is a poor guide to monitoring skill
caption: Each dot is one monitor setting: a model at one reasoning level. Higher catches more of the 500 backdoors; further left costs less per program at list price. Lines join a model's settings and the dashed line traces the best buys. Bars are 95% intervals.
notes: Control Tax (Terekhov et al., 2025) already plots a cost-vs-safety frontier for 13 monitors at a 5% budget. What's ours is reasoning effort as a second dial, current models, and exact-budget accounting.
Sonnet 5.5 is labelled untrusted monitoring in our runs, but older models wrote the code it reads, so there's no collusion. Treat it as a reference point, not a trusted monitor a lab would deploy.

Costs are list price times tokens, after Marnick's fixes: cached calls count, and GLM-5.3 is priced at the discounted rate it is billed at. GLM-5.3's effort=none run is left off: it is max in disguise.
